name: Passage Engine
description: A graph of text, and the state that makes the same passage read differently the second time. Passages are nodes; links are edges; and interpolation is what separates interactive fiction from a gamebook — a passage that can name the character you spared reads as written for you. The engine owns traversal and rendering-of-text only: which links are OFFERED is ui.choice_consequence's decision against its flags, which is why the two are separate contracts rather than one big one. A link to a passage that does not exist is refused at load rather than at reach, because discovering a dead link mid-story costs the player their place.

inputs.name: passages
inputs.description: Passage nodes keyed by id, each with text and outgoing links. Required — this is the story.

inputs.name: interpolationDelimiters
inputs.description: Markers around state references inside passage text.

inputs.name: rejectDeadLinks
inputs.description: Whether links to missing passages are refused on load rather than on arrival.

outputs.name: currentPassage
outputs.description: The passage being read, after interpolation.

outputs.name: availableLinks
outputs.description: Links offered from here, after conditions.
